# What & Why

![][image1]

## **What & Why**

### Customization versus Scale

SaaS software has scaled to billions of users, unlocking efficiency and growth for the businesses that have adopted it. But by definition, scale requires software to generalise — platforms can’t build for every edge case, workflow, or niche business need. 

It’s not that leading platforms don’t want to serve every need, it’s that they can’t. As a result they invest heavily in developer APIs, app marketplaces, workflow builders, and low code tools. These help, but still require time, effort, and some technical ability, with every software ecosystem having its own learning curve. If users can code, they might try to write scripts or wire up APIs. If they can’t code, they’ll dig through static app directories, hope Zapier does enough, or give up and do tasks manually. The result is a long tail of unsolved problems, inefficient processes, and business logic that lives entirely outside of a platform’s software.

Most users know exactly what they want, and while there are tens of millions of developers in the world, the vast majority of software users are not software developers \- they’re operators, marketers, finance leads, support managers, sales leaders \- and asking them to pick endpoints or manage webhook retries doesn’t help. 

### Customization at Scale

[Javelin](https://withjavelin.com/) is an AI-powered builder that makes it possible for anyone to customize the software platforms they already use — without needing to write code or hire a developer. It takes an ecosystem-native approach, meaning it operates *inside* the platform itself, with deep awareness of how that platform works, how the user is currently using it, what data exists, and what the user has done before — Understanding the platform’s capabilities, the user’s data model, and the workflows already in place. It’s like having an always-on-call developer who knows your business, your tools, and your instance inside and out — and can instantly build what you need. It empowers all users to describe the outcome they want and instantly get a working solution. By dropping the effort to near zero, it drastically increases the velocity of problem-solving and customization, and helps users move faster with the systems they already rely on.

## **Where to Start**

### The Platform

Our initial platform needs to be:

* Highly extensible and well-documented (ie. granular API, native webhooks/eventing, machine auth, etc) that allows Javelin (as a 3rd party) to provide meaningful orchestration on behalf of the user.    
* Horizontal in nature, meaning they serve a wide range of business types and use cases.  
* Incomplete coverage across workflows their users need.  
* Equipped with distribution, meaning they don’t just have APIs, but also a packaging and delivery model (like an app marketplace) that makes it easy for users to discover, adopt, and trust new solutions.

Stripe fits this profile, and is one of the most popular, powerful and extensible web-based software platforms — but for many of its users, that power requires code, and Stripe cannot deliver all the niche features that its broad user base demands

### The User

Our initial target user — founders, owners, and ops leads inside small and growing companies — are a fit because:

* **They know exactly what they want** \- These users are close to the problem. They’re often founders, ops leads, or support/finance owners who deeply understand their workflows and pain points. They don’t need to be sold on the value of a solution — they already feel the friction every day.  
* **They have the authority to act** \- In small teams, there’s no approval chain or committee. These users can see a problem, decide to fix it, and immediately try something new. That makes them ideal for early adoption: short sales cycles, fast feedback loops, and clear ROI.  
* **They don’t have engineering resources to burn** \- Even if they can code or work with developers, it’s rarely worth the time. Engineering is always focused on product, not internal ops fixes or Stripe tweaks. The ruthless operator wants leverage without dependency.  
* **They’re already hacking together manual workarounds** \- They’re often operating in spreadsheets, Notion, or custom dashboards trying to patch together what Stripe (or any platform) won’t do out of the box. These are high-intent users — they’re already trying to solve the problem, just with bad tools.  
* **They prioritize speed over polish** \- They don’t need perfect design or complete coverage. They want something that works now, even if it’s 80%. That makes them a forgiving, action-biased early user base that will pressure-test and validate the AI builder fast.  
* **Are increasingly comfortable with AI,** especially founders of software companies and modern businesses, who are already using tools like ChatGPT or Claude in their daily workflows.

Founders, operations leads, and finance teams often know *exactly* how they want Stripe to behave for their business, but don’t have the time or technical resources to build custom apps, workflows, or dashboards. In short, they’re high-friction users with high agency — frustrated enough to want a solution, empowered enough to try one immediately, and underserved enough that even a partial win is a huge unlock.

These users don’t want “apps” — they want Stripe to work exactly the way they need it to, without waiting on a developer or compromising with a 3rd party tool. They want to fix broken internal workflows, automate manual processes, and customize Stripe to fit how they already run their business. 

### The Beachead

Intentionally narrow scope of internal-only customizations for how Stripe users operate. That means we don’t yet touch end-customer experiences (like Checkout or invoice emails), and we don’t require integrations with external systems (like NetSuite or Airtable). Instead, we focus on improving how Stripe works for the user, inside the Stripe Dashboard and across its platform \- It’s smaller scope than other areas, meaning faster to deliver and lower risk for users to test (ie. it’s not touching the user’s end customer) 

| Phase | Description | Focus |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| MVP | Internal-only customizations (just for the user’s Stripe account) | Fastest time to value |
| M2 | Internal workflows that connect Stripe to other systems | Adds complexity, still internal |
| M3 | End-customer facing logic (e.g. checkout customization) | Adds trust / safety risk |
| M4  | Third-party app creation \+ publishing, available to partners | Introduces public distribution, shareability |

Expansion into a next milestone will be based on observed user needs, meaning the above can (and likely will) change depending on what users are asking for (ie. they may request checkout customization earlier than expected). 

**M5 and Multi Ecosystem** \- Once Javelin proves the model inside Stripe, it expands to solve the same pain that exists in every major ecosystem — HubSpot, Shopify, QuickBooks, Salesforce, Atlassian, etc. — where users struggle to shape the platform to fit how their business actually runs. Each one represents a massive ecosystem of users waiting for simpler, smarter customization. Javelin becomes the layer that turns every ecosystem into one that truly adapts to its users.

## **Potential Use Cases**

| Problem / Pain | Feasible? | Constraints | Gaps to Fill |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Failed payment visibility & recovery workflows | Partial | Stripe controls retry logic. Can’t modify Smart Retries, only respond to failures. | Generate recovery dashboards, segment failed payments, suggest recovery workflows (alerts, tags, tasks). |
| Custom dashboards & internal views | Yes | Stripe dashboard doesn’t support user-created views natively; but app UIs can display panels. | Scaffold visual dashboards from Stripe data (filters, aggregations, visualizations). Allow embedding in Stripe App Drawer. |
| Bulk metadata/tag editing | Yes | Some rate limits apply. Must manage pagination and field validation. | Generate bulk editing tools in the App UI. Suggest batch operations and confirm before applying. |
| Context linking between related objects | Yes | Stripe doesn’t provide native “relationship maps.” Must infer links  | Use AI to auto-generate object relationship views (relational panel / breadcrumb-style UI) in App extension. |
| Workflow automation inside Stripe | Partial | Stripe Workflows only 12 steps, 1 trigger, no async. Apps can bypass via custom logic, but must avoid conflict. | Generate logic that supplements or replaces Stripe Workflows when more complex behavior is needed.  |
| Dispute response & tracking tools | Yes | Stripe allows evidence upload via API, but not UI customization of native dispute screen. | Scaffold internal dispute UI with status, evidence suggestions, and templates to respond. |
| Metadata syncing across Stripe products | Yes | No automatic metadata sync across objects in Stripe today. You must do it manually via API. | Generate logic that listens for object changes and mirrors metadata across linked entities (e.g. customer → invoice). |
| Undo / rollback / change history | Partial | Stripe doesn’t offer versioning. You can only “overwrite” values (e.g. reset metadata). Some changes (e.g. state transitions) can’t be undone. | Builder maintains a changelog, versioning layer in the app backend. Offers rollback options for safe changes only. |
| Logs / traceability / diagnostics | Yes | Stripe’s log viewer is dev-focused. No user-level trace across business logic or workflow chain. | Builder provides high-level activity feed per customer/workflow: what ran, what failed, what triggered it, etc. |

# Open Thinking

**A Better Economic Model**  
Users will go from buying apps, to paying for outcomes powered by more modular tools. Platforms and their partners will go from monetizing more static products to monetizing smaller bits of the participation in critical workflows. This leads to new usage-based models (pay per automation, per API call, per task solved), where that alignment will allow for “Day 1” monetization for an ecosystem, which simply wasn’t possible before.

**Differentiation and Ecosystem Native**  
Javelin isn’t just ecosystem-native in terms of distribution — we treat each platform as a true development platform. That means building deeply into the platform’s design system, data model, and UI components so Javelin feels like a seamless extension of the core product. Stripe, Shopify, or HubSpot aren’t just channels for reaching users — they’re the foundations to build on.

**Stripe Balance Pay**  
Balance Pay allows a Stripe user to pay another Stripe user using the funds from their Stripe account. It’s a win-win, in that it’s lower cost for both users, and higher margin for Stripe. The first use case is for SaaS platforms to allow their users to pay their SaaS fees via Stripe Balance \- but given Apps are built on Connect as a programming model, there may be a way for a user to pay apps fees using their Stripe Balance.

**Webhooks as an Escape Hatch**  
For users in the sense that it allows those users that are technical to build additional logic that can then respond to events, and for Stripe in that enables them NOT to build every feature and push that customization on the user The gap here is that the non-technical users that can't leverage webhooks to easily solve problems.	

# GTM

## Strategy \- Two Layers 

### Layer 1: Direct Users 

* Reaching end users where they complain: Stripe Community, LinkedIn, founder groups.   
* Focused on immediate user interaction and acquisition.

### Layer 2: Platform and Ecosystem Amplification 

* Stripe employees and others in the Ecosystem as users and champions.  
* Support, Sales Engineers, Partner Engineers, AEs, Pro Serve, RevOps and PaymentOps consultants. 

### Flywheel

* The 2 layers have potential to reenforce each other where:  
  * Stripe champions mention Javelin in sales calls → users try it → success stories → more champions.   
  * Direct users provide case studies → convince stakeholders → accelerate adoption.

### App Marketplace Listing

Target: 

* Stripe's built-in distribution channel for all Stripe users.

Action Steps:

1. Go to stripe.com/docs/stripe-apps/submit-app  
2. Complete required items:  
   * App manifest file (stripe-app.json)  
   * OAuth scopes request (ask for: read\_customers, read\_subscriptions, write\_customers)  
   * Security self-assessment questionnaire  
   * Privacy policy page (use Iubenda, $29)  
   * Support email with \<2h SLA (hello@withjavelin.com)  
   * App icon 512x512px  
   * Screenshots: 1280x800px, show 3 clean template UIs  
   * Listing copy: "Workflow automation for Stripe. No code. Fixes gaps Stripe doesn't support."

Post-Launch:

* Email all users/prospects: "Javelin is now in the Stripe App Marketplace"  
* Post on r/stripe linking to App Marketplace
